findings.title: Detached-HEAD refusal is specified in Task 3 but never wired or tested at the command level
"Fails the same way with the same command" contradicts the task's own test expectations
findings.description: Description: The slice's functional success criterion states that a branch whose host sha differs from local "fails the same way **with the same command**" as an unpushed branch. The task file is internally inconsistent about what "the same command" means: Task 6.1/6.2 say the two refusals name *different* commands (`git push -u <remote> <head>` for missing, line 139, vs `git push <remote> <head>` for behind, line 147), with the explicit success note "the two refusals name different commands" (line 149). The design's D2 is on the task's side (it specifies the two different fixes, and D2 is the decision the design review PASSed). So the criterion's "same command" reads as shorthand for "the same refusal treatment (before any write, names the fix)" — but taken literally, it is unsatisfiable by the specified implementation, and a junior implementer cross-referencing the criteria could "fix" the tasks to print one command for both, regressing D2's different-fixes rule. Fix: reword or annotate the criterion (or have the task file note the reading) so the two readings cannot diverge.

findings.title: No **Commit:** markers anywhere in the file
findings.description: Description: Verified by grep — there are no plain `**Commit:**` lines. This is acceptable: CLAUDE.md requires committing "at least once per task," which the effort-tagged, checkbox-driven structure satisfies, and the slice has no NFR that would require a load test or CI gating. No action needed; noting only that if commit points are ever wanted, the natural seams are after Task 4 (refactor), 9 (deterministic core), and 13 (command wired, all fake-tested) — the tested points before live work in Task 16.

findings.title: Task 2.2's fixture assertion must hold for non-task markdown too
findings.description: Description: The real-file test asserts "both groups are non-empty **and** their counts sum to the file's checkbox count." Any real task file in `project-documents/user/tasks/` that contains checked and unchecked items will satisfy both clauses, so 2.2's fallback choice (`384-tasks.post-findings-to-the-pr.md`) is safe, and this file at test time will contain all-checked items (task-checker checks items as they go — note its own 2.2 is likely unchecked, keeping the unchecked group non-empty). No fix required; flagging so the implementer doesn't "helpfully" tighten the assertion.
